youtube.title: Rust Day 6: Integers & Floats Explained (i32, u8, f64) 🦀 #Shorts

scenes.say: Rust, day six. Which number type should you use?

scenes.heading: Integer sizes
scenes.say: Integers come in 8 to 128 bits. i is signed, so it can be negative. u is unsigned. The default is i32.
scenes.captions: Integers come in 8 to 128 bits. i is signed, so it can be negative. u is unsigned. The default is i32.

scenes.heading: Numbers in code
scenes.say: a is forty two, an i32 by default. b is a u8, up to two fifty five. underscores just help reading. three point five is an f64, and e is an f32 because we asked.
scenes.captions: a is 42, an i32 by default. b is a u8, up to 255. Underscores just help reading. 3.5 is an f64, and e is an f32 because we asked.

scenes.heading: Run it
scenes.caption: the _ is gone in the output
scenes.say: Run it: no underscores in the output, and two point zero prints as two.
scenes.captions: Run it: no underscores in the output, and 2.0 prints as 2.

scenes.heading: u8 range
scenes.label: i8: -128 to 127
scenes.say: Eight bits: u8 is zero to two fifty five, i8 is minus 128 to 127.
scenes.captions: 8 bits: u8 is 0 to 255, i8 is -128 to 127.

scenes.heading: Division
scenes.say: Careful: integer seven divided by two is three, the fraction is dropped. with floats it's three point five. percent gives the remainder: one.
scenes.captions: Careful: integer 7 / 2 is 3, the fraction is dropped. With floats it's 3.5. % gives the remainder: 1.

scenes.heading: Common mistake
scenes.say: Now the classic mistake: adding an i32 to an f64.

scenes.heading: The real error
scenes.caption: E0277: no i32 + f64
scenes.say: Error E0277: cannot add f64 to i32. Rust never converts silently, so write a as f64.
scenes.captions: Error E0277: cannot add f64 to i32. Rust never converts silently, so write a as f64.

scenes.heading: Recap
scenes.say: Recap: i signed, u unsigned, defaults i32 and f64, and convert before mixing.
